Role Description: Dynamic row-level security. A user sees the departments of the current structure that the synthetic user map gives them, and so only their departments' outturn. Plan is published by Spending Review group, so a user sees the plan of a group only when every department of the group is one of theirs. A user in no row of the map sees nothing. The NHS trust accounts follow the same filter through the provider's department (only a user mapped to the Department of Health and Social Care sees them), and so do the hand-keyed consolidated figures. The allocation of the Cabinet Office administration budget follows the same department filter through its bridge; its pool is not filtered, because a user who sees a department's weight and allocated amount can divide to get it. The audit and control tables are not restricted in this role.
Row Filter:
CONTAINS (
    'User Department (synthetic)',
    'User Department (synthetic)'[User Principal Name], USERPRINCIPALNAME (),
    'User Department (synthetic)'[Department Key], 'Department (current structure)'[Department Key]
)

Row-level security and object-level security in one role (the engine refuses a row-level role combined with a separate object-level one). The same department and plan filters as Department Analyst. The NHS trust accounts and the consolidated figures follow the same filter and the identity of each provider (name, code, region, sector, years and successor) is hidden. The allocation follows the same department filter; its pool is not filtered, because a user who sees a department's weight and allocated amount can divide to get it. The audit and control tables are hidden, the organisation names and version history are hidden, and the line-level detail of the data-quality findings is hidden. A measure that reads a hidden object returns an error, not a blank. The pay bridge follows the same department filter; the organisation-level paybill detail is hidden (the organisation names and codes, the organisation key of the pay bridge, and the workforce coverage table).
